brief.headline: Kyiv drone plants struck; Ukraine fires Defense Minister Fedorov
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels celebrated a broad Russian strike wave on Kyiv drone-assembly plants and Black Sea shipping, while dwelling on the political fallout from Ukraine's dismissal of Defense Minister Fedorov. Tone was mixed—triumphant on strikes, defensive on Ukrainian drone attacks reaching Belgorod, Crimea and Black Sea vessels.

developments.title: Russia strikes Kyiv drone plants and Black Sea shipping
developments.body: Channels claim Russian strikes hit Kyiv drone-production sites (naming RAPID and Kyiv-1), Odesa ports and gas stations, with Geran drones striking cargo ships in Chornomorsk and Dnipro-Bug ports—four vessels claimed hit in one day. Claims are channel-sourced and unconfirmed; framed as reciprocal to Ukrainian strikes on Russian tankers.

developments.title: Ukraine dismisses Defense Minister Fedorov, sparking crisis claims
developments.body: Multiple channels report Zelensky fired Defense Minister Fedorov after six months, framing it variously as Western-orchestrated signaling, a Syrsky/General Staff power struggle, or removal for auditing corruption. Kotsnews names SBU chief Khmara as successor, alleging war-crimes involvement—all unverified framing.

developments.title: Ukrainian drones hit Belgorod, Crimea and Black Sea vessels
developments.body: Channels report—with negative sentiment—Ukrainian FPV drones striking four Belgorod municipalities and expanding attacks south of Kerch Strait against Russian Black Sea shipping, claiming a 55% AIS reduction. Two Majors also cites a terrorism case after the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant's chief engineer was killed.

developments.title: FSB claims foiled GUR Monaco assassination and terror plots
developments.body: Channels amplify claimed FSB counterterror successes: an alleged GUR-orchestrated Monaco attack on a Ukrainian oligarch, and a GUR officer named Zhikovich accused of recruiting Islamists and planning Crimea Bridge bombings. Also cited: minors detained in Kursk (15) and elsewhere for alleged recruitment. All MoD/FSB-sourced and unconfirmed.

developments.title: Crimea fuel crisis: gasoline tops 200 rubles/liter
developments.body: Two Majors reports a Crimea fuel crisis with gasoline prices jumping 30 rubles in one week, exceeding 200 rubles per liter—a rare negative domestic-economy signal amplified by a major channel.

developments.title: Lopsided body exchange: 501 Ukrainian for 31 Russian
developments.body: Channels report a body exchange in which Russia handed over 501 Ukrainian bodies and received 31 Russian soldiers' remains; WarGonzo cites a cumulative 1023-to-64 ratio since June, framed as evidence of heavy Ukrainian losses.

narrative_watch.title: Fedorov firing framed as Kyiv political implosion
narrative_watch.body: Channels converge on Ukraine's defense minister dismissal as a Western-driven or infighting-driven crisis, variously spun as corruption exposure, US/Trump pressure, or elite resource-grabbing—maximally destabilizing framing.

narrative_watch.title: Strikes framed as reciprocal retaliation
narrative_watch.body: Russian strikes on Ukrainian cargo ships and ports are repeatedly justified as tit-for-tat responses to Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian tankers, casting Russia as reactive.

narrative_watch.title: Digital sovereignty grievance over app removals
narrative_watch.body: Google Play's removal of 20 Russian apps (VK, MAX, Mail) under EU sanctions triggers a narrative of Russia's vulnerability in the digital domain and Western tech coercion.

mood_lines.text: Uniformly triumphant across 14 posts celebrating strikes on Kyiv drone plants, Odesa ports and Black Sea cargo ships.
Still net-positive but cooling; more neutral posts on Sumy/Kupyansk fighting alongside claimed advances near Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk.
Turned sharply negative as channels acknowledge Belgorod, Crimea and Black Sea shipping strikes; sentiment dropped 36 points.
Broadly hostile: Sea Breeze exercises, UK Nightfall missile, app removals and Taiwan drone-battery supplies all framed as escalation.
Notably darker: Crimea fuel crisis, lopsided body exchanges and child-recruitment cases offset positive MoD inspection coverage.
Still deeply negative but improved as channels gleefully cover Ukrainian dysfunction—Fedorov firing, GUR plots and SBU arrests.

flag_texts.title: Frontline optimism cools (-33)
flag_texts.body: Frontline sentiment fell to net +67 as coverage shifted toward neutral situational updates on Sumy and Kupyansk rather than unambiguous advance claims.

flag_texts.title: Ukraine strikes on Russia sour (-36)
flag_texts.body: Sentiment dropped to net -25 as channels reported Ukrainian FPV attacks on four Belgorod municipalities, expanded Black Sea vessel strikes with a claimed 55% AIS reduction, and the killing of a Zaporizhzhia plant engineer.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal mood darkens (-38)
flag_texts.body: Net fell to -38 driven by the Crimea fuel crisis (gasoline above 200 rubles/liter), a lopsided 501-to-31 body exchange, and reports of minors recruited for sabotage.

flag_texts.title: Criticism sentiment improves (+29)
flag_texts.body: Despite remaining deeply negative (-71), the topic rose as channels celebrated perceived Ukrainian dysfunction—Fedorov's dismissal, alleged GUR terror plots and SBU arrests.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation rumours across two channels
flag_texts.body: Two channels (Poddubny, Kotsnews) posted on mobilisation-adjacent themes, both covering the Russian Defense Minister's inspection of Central grouping forces praising improved drone coordination—positive rather than alarmist framing.

flag_texts.title: Criticism of Putin absent
flag_texts.body: No posts directly criticizing Putin appeared today; the watchlist item remained quiet across all ten monitored channels.
